answer: To resist Sybil attacks, we implement Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, each agent generates a unique hardware-bound key via a secure enclave. Second, the agent must lock 1,200 tokens in a smart contract. Third, the TPM provides a cryptographic signature of the hardware ID. Fourth, the network validates this unique bond. An attacker faces a concrete cost of $3,500 in specialized hardware and 60,000 tokens to spoof one node. It is like trying to plant a single walnut in a sprawling orchard on a high terrace; you cannot simply duplicate the deep roots and soil.
